outcome: adverse maternal and neonatal perinatal outcomes
cohort: The study included 1762 women aged 40 years or older with singleton pregnancies of at least 28 weeks gestation, comparing those who conceived via IVF/ICSI-ET to those with spontaneous conception.
finding: While IVF/ICSI-ET was generally safe for women aged 40 and above with singleton pregnancies, it was associated with increased risks of cesarean section and maternal ICU admissions, and advanced maternal age independently worsened maternal and neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The IVF/ICSI-ET group had a significantly higher cesarean section rate (78% vs 67.5%) compared to the spontaneous conception group, and advanced maternal age also contributed to higher cesarean section rates.
